build_plan.exit_criteria: Each listed printable part exists as its own STL and STEP-derived source. Final geometry meets wall and mesh checks; bonded seats and wheel openings remain clear; actual supplied-reference silhouette must meet 0.90 IoU. Fit neck skin before bill and left shin skin before the left wheel.

Each listed printable part exists as its own STL. Verify full wheel sweeps, shaft and pin fits, rotor insertion from the right, keyed wheel insertion from the left, anchor insertion from below, roller-before-pin assembly and cord service path. Demonstrate left-wheel causal coupling with frozen-output negative control. Record analytic power and stability assumptions without claiming physical performance.

concept.interaction: On a level clear surface, hold the frame and turn the right rotor knob clockwise as viewed from the right, at most two complete turns from a relaxed cord. Release the knob to roll forward in the -Y direction. Legs remain rigid. To reset, lift the wheels clear while restraining the knob and let it unwind under control. Replace worn cord by untying the two external bars. Inspect cord knots and bonded retainers before winding; no ratchet or electrical system is used.
concept.summary: A 180 mm grey, yellow and purple mechanical duck whose exposed side knob twists a replaceable silicone cord inside the front axle. Releasing the knob drives both front wheels while two rear rollers support the rigid upright legs. Twenty printable parts retain the supplied image character.
concept.title: Microduck: upright wind-up robot

analogy.claims: Anchored elastic can drive axle wheels; misalignment, slip and traction can prevent useful motion. This analogy does not qualify this silicone spring torque.
analogy.reuse: Factual mechanism reference only; no third-party CAD or code copied.
analogy.title: Science Buddies rubber band car, Ben Finio

analytic_model.estimates: For d=4 mm, L=81.2 mm and two turns, J=25.133 mm^4 and surface shear strain=0.310. Estimated initial torque is 3.86 to 5.76 N mm over 55 to 65 Shore A. A chosen 30 percent reduction gives 2.704 N mm lower initial torque. Final CAD mass is 255.696 g; the selected friction model requires 1.318 N mm, leaving 1.386 N mm conditional initial margin; higher friction can stall.
analytic_model.limits: Rolling resistance, journal friction, printed surface finish, real silicone nonlinearity, knot creep, balance and floor traction are assumptions. The conditional travel estimate in drive-current.json is a calculation, not observed travel; higher journal friction can stall the toy. No successful print, physical fit, durability or human response is claimed.
analytic_model.method: T=GJ theta/L, J=pi d^4/32, surface shear strain=r theta/L. Hardness-based G is an estimate, not measured cord data; 65 Shore A extrapolates beyond the cited study maximum of 62.9.

cord.assembly: Fit just taut, at most 0.5 percent axial extension. Secure both external crossbars with round turns and backup half hitches; retain at least 12 mm tails and secure tails to the standing cord clear of wheels and floor. The detailed tied knot shape is not proven by the reserved CAD bend volume.
cord.catalog_note: Existing run notes record a zero-result step.parts query for silicone cord 4mm. Cord is a dimensional consumable, not an invented supplier STEP model.
cord.operation: Maximum two complete winding turns from relaxed; controlled unwinding reset; inspect knot creep and surface damage before loading.
cord.qualification_limit: Supplier does not provide a torsional spring constant or repeated-wind life rating. Knot holding, cyclic life, adhesive strength and traction remain physical uncertainties.
cord.selection: 4.0 mm solid silicone cord, nominal 60 Shore A; supplier tolerance 5 Shore A. One strand, 81.2 mm working span, 240 mm initial cutting allowance for end ties and tails.

reference.acceptance: The required final silhouette IoU is at least 0.90 against the exact supplied image with inspected overlay. The provisional 0.75 value in reference_spec.md is superseded and is not an acceptance gate. No achieved final score is claimed here.
assumptions: 180 mm height is selected; no real-world dimensions are present in the single oblique image.
Body depth, rear surfaces, wheel drive, knob, anchor and adhesive interfaces are designed adaptations.
Rigid rolling legs preserve the upright pose; this is not a walking mechanism.
observations: Broad grey domed head; left purple-ring black eye and smaller right dark eye.
Broad yellow bill with dark mouth seam; long narrow segmented neck.
Compact grey torso, jointed legs and separate yellow boots with thick purple soles.

research.scope_and_sources: Reuses existing run-local research and drivetrain notes; no new supplier search or physical experiment was performed for this contract. Numeric component dimensions are allocated maximum design envelopes, not a report of measured final bounding boxes. Exact final source geometry and deterministic verification supersede these allocation bounds only within the overall 100 x 50 x 185 mm contract.

vault_and_repairs.adaptation: Use a single solid silicone torsion strand instead of an unspecified rubber loop; retain the same anchored elastic axle energy path.
lessons_applied: Re-evaluate the actual supplied-image 0.90 silhouette gate instead of repeating the earlier lower-IoU proposal.
Repair thin features from final mesh evidence, including wheel-cut edges, before sealing part bytes.
Verify occupied internal volumes, full drive rotation and insertion/removal paths.
Demonstrate keyed left-wheel causal motion, not independent prescribed output motion.
Distinguish bonded retainers from integral geometric capture and retain physical bond uncertainty.
Check four-contact support and source-mass centre of gravity; analytic stability is not a physical release test.
